DIPLOMAT QUEUED THIS ISSUE AT A PIPELINE SYNC, and your turn may have come long after. Before you touch anything, look for an open PR that already fixes it: `gh pr list --repo software-mansion/argent --state open --search ENG-42`. If one names ENG-42, stop there: change nothing, post nothing, and report it as skipped.

ONLY A REAL BUG REPORT IS IN SCOPE. Decide what this issue actually is: a bug report describes something that behaves wrongly. A feature request, enhancement proposal, design discussion, question, support request or wishlist item is explicitly OUT OF SCOPE and must not be worked, however easy it looks — stop there and report it as skipped. When it is ambiguous, treat it as out of scope and say so rather than implementing something nobody asked you to.

Build a CONCRETE REPRODUCTION from the report before you change anything — precise inputs / steps → the wrong behaviour, run for real — so you have proof the bug exists and proof of what it does. Then develop the fix, and re-run that SAME reproduction to confirm it lands. Then put your own fix through the review moves with a swarm of agents (3–8) — claims vs code (every comment, docstring, description, error message, type, test name and README line the change touches or silently falsifies still tells the truth about the code), nearest twin (each changed rule, constant, guard, mapping or message agrees with whatever does the same job elsewhere: the other platform, the other call site, the other arm of the same branch), non-happy paths (errors, timeouts, cancellation, partial success and missing input: what the caller is told, what state is left behind, and above all whether anything reports success for work it did not do), inputs (empty, non-finite, boundary, misspelled or extra keys, alternate spellings, and shapes only one platform produces, including the message each one gets), reachability both ways (whether each branch or guard can actually fire or is shadowed by an earlier check, and whether its value reaches the consumer it was written for), and what outlives the call (processes, temp files, caches, device state, two callers racing one file, and every timeout on the path summed against the budget the code claims) — plus the absence pass, which finds what is missing by comparing against a reference: a sibling that has it, prose that promises it, symmetry (spawn/reap, open/close, write/delete, set/reset), and the mutation (break a constant, delete a branch or invert a condition, then run the tests: if they stay green, nothing pins that code). Treat what the swarm returns as leads, not verdicts: confirm each against the code, fix what is real, and keep dispatching fresh swarms until one full pass comes back clean.

Hold to this bar throughout. DONE MEANS OBSERVABLE PROOF, never "should work", and you say which verification you ran. Fix the CLASS, not the instance — search the repo for every other call site, sibling backend or adjacent path of the same shape and fix them together, or name each one you are leaving and why. Bring every piece of prose the change touches into agreement with the new behaviour, and write it as a description of the code as it now stands, never as a narration of what changed. Delete anything the fix made unreachable. And run the project's own checks — format, lint, typecheck, tests, build — before you call it done.

AN ISSUE YOU CANNOT REPRODUCE IS NOT A FAILURE OF THE RUN — it is a result, and it has to be reported as one. Never paper over it with a speculative change: no fix goes in on a bug you were unable to make happen. Say exactly what you tried (the steps, the version, the environment) and what you observed instead, so the gap is something I can act on.

Deliver the fix as its own focused pull request, opened as a DRAFT (`gh pr create --draft`), and never mark it ready yourself. It closes the issue it fixes: put a closing reference (`Fixes ENG-42`) in its description, and give it a title and description that name the defect and quote the evidence — the reproduction that proved the bug, and the same reproduction re-run clean after the fix. SHIP A REGRESSION TEST WITH THE FIX, one that pins the exact behaviour it corrected: you established the wrong value when you reproduced the bug and the right one when you confirmed the fix, so assert the right one in a way the wrong one would VIOLATE (an exact value, count, order, type or status code — never an incidental property like `>= 1` or `contains something`, which the unfixed code already satisfied). Do not undo or weaken the fix to check that; argue it from the reproduction you already captured. RIGHT BEFORE you open it, verify it is NOT a DUPLICATE of an existing open PR — this issue may already have one, and other agents are working the repo's other issues alongside you: enumerate the repo's open PRs and compare their ACTUAL CODE, not their titles or descriptions (those routinely mislead), reading each plausible candidate's real diff with `gh pr diff <n>`. If one already lands the same fix, do NOT open a duplicate: skip it and tell me which PR already covers it.

Diplomat attribution tag — a REQUIRED exception to the no-attribution rule, for GitHub commentary only. Do NOT tag PR titles — leave every pull-request title exactly as you would write it. End every pull-request DESCRIPTION with a footer: after the body, a blank line, a horizontal rule on its own line (`---`), a blank line, then this exact last line — `<sub>Made by Diplomat. Like what you're seeing? [Give it a try](https://github.com/latekvo/Diplomat).</sub>`. In that footer the word Diplomat is PLAIN TEXT (not a link); ONLY "Give it a try" is a Markdown link, pointing to https://github.com/latekvo/Diplomat. For every standalone comment you post instead (an issue comment, or a review / reply comment), BEGIN it with the exact prefix `\[[Diplomat](https://github.com/latekvo/Diplomat)\]: `, copied character for character — the `\[` and `\]` are literal brackets, only the word Diplomat is a Markdown link (to https://github.com/latekvo/Diplomat), anything after that link is plain text, and a colon and a space close it — followed by the text you would otherwise have written, so it renders as "[Diplomat]: <your text>".
